title: Lesson 31 - Data Lake Objects vs Data Model Objects and Mapping Streams to the Model
description: Model data in Data 360., focused on the difference between data lake objects and data model objects, the mapping between them, required keys, and the ingestion order that makes mapping work.

questions.question: How does a Data Lake Object relate to a Data Model Object?
options: The Data Lake Object is the harmonized model object.
The Data Lake Object is the raw, stream-shaped table that must be mapped onto a Data Model Object to become model data.
They are two names for the same object.
A Data Lake Object cannot be mapped to a model object.
questions.explanation: A DLO is the staging layer that mirrors the source; mapping its fields to a DMO turns them into model attributes. They are distinct layers, and mapping a DLO to a DMO is exactly how data reaches the model.

questions.question: A stream loaded successfully, but its records never appear in identity resolution. What is the most likely cause?
options: The Data Lake Object has too many fields.
The Individual ID was never mapped from a populated source column.
The org reached a Data Model Object limit.
questions.explanation: Even with data loaded, an unmapped or empty Individual ID means the record cannot join to a person, so identity resolution skips it. Field count, a DMO limit, and a disabled ruleset do not match the described symptom.

questions.question: An architect must use data already ingested in a Data Lake Object for a second Data Model Object without reloading it. What do they do?
options: Add a second mapping from the existing Data Lake Object to the target Data Model Object.
Query the DLO and reload it through an API.
questions.explanation: You can map an existing DLO to an additional DMO without re-ingesting, which reuses the staged data. Re-ingesting, cloning, and API reloads either duplicate data or waste effort for a result the mapping step already provides.
